referents.why: 'you refuse' is inside the LORD's message to Pharaoh, which continues across the verse break; the addressee is Pharaoh.
referents.category: second person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'I will plague' is the LORD speaking in the same message; Exo.7.26#w2 is the LORD named in the previous verse (the same person as the inner speaker w14).
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'your country' is the addressee's; the addressee is Pharaoh.

links.why: the infinitive 'to let them go' completes the verb 'refuse'; purpose is excluded for that.
links.category: infinitive completing a verb of refusal

links.why: the infinitive is the object of 'refuse', a clause nested in a role of another clause.
the link runs the wrong way: the condition is the destination and the consequence is the source.
'but if you refuse' is the condition on 'here, I am about to strike'.
the condition and its consequence are already joined by the if-link; a plain 'and' adds nothing.
'here!' introduces the consequence, which continues in a waw-joined participle.

groups.why: the 'if' clause and the clause it conditions; cl3 is a separate part of the speech.
the LORD's quoted message continues into this verse; a conditional said by the speaker is a part of the turn as a whole group.
